I can see where individual religious belief may cause conflict significant enough to provide for an individuals refusal on religious grounds to provide this right/benefit/privilege to a citizen, however the institution itself should not be exempt.

I'm recommending coop games but I don't know if they all have LAN

• Monaco: What's Yours is Mine would be my first suggestion aside from what's already on your list. Co-op heist game with distinct classes and fun gameplay. No LAN, but tolerable split-screen if you have a large enough screen. All four players occupy the same screen, similar to Diablo.
  • Borderlands 1 and 2 (and pre-sequel) are good suggestions if you haven't played them as a group yet. Humorous shooter with RPG elements
  • I haven't played this one, but Tidalis is a co-op puzzler with an interesting description: http://www.co-optimus.com/game/1554/pc/tidalis.html
  • Dungeon Defenders is a wave based trap and combat game that support 4 player LAN play
  • Terraria and Minecraft are options if you like creating things
  • Tom Clancy's H.A.W.X. is a good co-op flight game that's accessible for players unfamiliar with flight games
  • Call of Duty: Black Ops 3 actually has an enjoyable custom campaign, custom classes in campaign, and two different zombie modes (one of them replaces enemies in the campaign with zombies; the other mode is wave-based)
  • Dying Light recently gained an enhanced edition with a ton of new content added to their already rich co-op campaign. If your idea of surviving the zombie apocalypse includes parkour, this is the one for you.

As an additional resource, I'd check out Co-Optimus' System Picker that will let you find co-op games by system and feature. I set the filters to "PC", "At least 4 players", and "LAN Support" and then sorted by review score or user rating. There are a lot of games there that I'm unfamiliar with (I play on my Xbox One) but they all look like enjoyable game night games.

Kudos for having Torchlight 2 on there. You didn't rule out Diablo, so 2 or 3 are both good LAN party games -- the former is pretty easy to find these days, and requires no internet connection, because reasons. I really like spinning up just about any of the Command and Conquer games for LAN parties, but my favorite by far is CnC3: Kane's Wrath -- also pretty easy to find, with no "always on" requirements. If you want a slower paced RTS, try Sins of a Solar Empire: Rebellion -- same stipulations, but I'd recommend plunking down for it, just because Stardock is awesome.
Oh yeah: Sanctum 2. It's a wave-based combat and trap thing very similar to Dungeon Defenders, but with robots, guns, etc. I just noticed it's for sale on Steam @ $3.75. Can't lose at that price.
